facts.statement: Platecarpus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous, with a possible record from the late Campanian.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, Possible late Campanian record

facts.statement: The genus Platecarpus was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1869.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Cope, 1869

facts.statement: Fossils of Platecarpus have been found in the United States, and possibly in Belgium, Australia, and Africa.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the United States and possibly in Belgium, Australia, and Africa

facts.statement: Evidence from a well-preserved specimen indicates Platecarpus ate moderate-sized fish, while hypotheses suggest it also consumed squid and ammonites.
facts.quote: A well-preserved specimen of Platecarpus shows that it fed on moderate-sized fish, and it has been hypothesized to have fed on squid and ammonites as well

facts.statement: Research suggests Platecarpus swam with powerful, fast movements similar to modern sharks rather than in an eel-like fashion.
facts.quote: another study suggests that it swam more like modern sharks

facts.statement: Isotopic analysis of teeth suggests Platecarpus may have occasionally entered freshwater environments, similar to modern sea snakes.
facts.quote: Isotopic analysis on teeth specimens has suggested that this genus and Clidastes may have entered freshwater occasionally, just like modern sea snakes

facts.statement: A complete specimen (LACM 128319) indicates Platecarpus reached lengths of 5.57 to 5.67 meters and weighed approximately 548 kilograms.
facts.quote: A complete specimen LACM 128319 shows that it grew up to 5.57-5.67 m long and weighed around 548 kg

facts.statement: Platecarpus is characterized by a short skull and fewer teeth than other mosasaurs, with around 10 teeth in each dentary.
facts.quote: This genus is characterized by a short skull, and has fewer teeth than any other mosasaur (around 10 teeth in each dentary)

facts.statement: The specimen LACM 128319 preserves material within the scleral ring that may represent the retina of the eye.
facts.quote: LACM 128319 preserves matter within the scleral ring that may possibly be the retina of the eye

facts.statement: The specimen LACM 128319 preserves a respiratory tube in the form of cartilaginous tracheal rings.
facts.quote: The respiratory tube is also known in LACM 128319, preserved as cartilaginous tracheal rings

facts.statement: Preserved respiratory structures indicate that Platecarpus and other mosasaurs possessed two functional lungs.
facts.quote: This is an indication that Platecarpus and other mosasaurs had two functional lungs

facts.statement: Skin impressions preserved in the specimen LACM 128319 include both soft impressions and phosphate material.
facts.quote: Skin impressions are known from Platecarpus, preserved in LACM 128319 as soft impressions and phosphate material

facts.statement: The scales on the tail of Platecarpus were taller and larger than the scales on the rest of its body.
facts.quote: The caudal scales on the tail are taller and larger than those of the rest of the body

facts.statement: A preserved portion of the digestive tract in a Platecarpus specimen contains remains of mid-sized fish.
facts.quote: Part of the digestive tract is also preserved and is filled with mid-sized fish remains

facts.statement: Platecarpus fossils are found in Smoky Hill Chalk rocks dating from the late Santonian to the early Campanian.
facts.quote: Platecarpus fossils have been found in rocks that date back to the late Santonian through the early Campanian in the Smoky Hill Chalk

facts.statement: Scientists now consider Platecarpus to be a paraphyletic genus.
facts.quote: scientists now consider it to be of the paraphyletic genus

facts.statement: Platecarpus is considered monotypic because P. coryphaeus and P. ictericus were synonymized with the type species P. tympaniticus.
facts.quote: Platecarpus is considered monotypic, as P. coryphaeus and P. ictericus were synonymized with its type species, P. tympaniticus

facts.statement: Platecarpus had less robust teeth than tylosaurs, suggesting it fed on smaller or softer prey like small fish and squid.
facts.quote: Compared to the tylosaurs, plioplatecarpine mosasaurs had much less robust teeth, suggesting that they fed on smaller (or softer) prey such as small fish and squid

facts.statement: Platecarpus likely swam using a shark-like method rather than the eel-like lateral undulation typical of other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: the deep caudal fin of Platecarpus suggests that it swam more like a shark

facts.statement: The downturned caudal vertebrae indicate that Platecarpus possessed a crescent-shaped tail fluke.
facts.quote: The downturned caudal vertebrae of Platecarpus suggest it had a crescent-shaped tail fluke.

facts.statement: Platecarpus utilized carangiform locomotion, where the tail base remained stable while the fluke and back undulated.
facts.quote: This form of movement is known as carangiform locomotion.

facts.statement: Platecarpus had small, similarly shaped body scales that stiffened its trunk to improve hydrodynamic efficiency.
facts.quote: The structure of the scales of Platecarpus may have been another adaptation toward a marine lifestyle.

facts.statement: Platecarpus likely fed on fish, squid, and ammonites.
facts.quote: Platecarpus probablemente se alimentaba de peces, calamares y ammonites.

facts.statement: An exceptionally preserved specimen (LACM 128319) shows skin impressions, nasal pigment, bronchial tubes, and a high caudal fin.
facts.quote: Un ejemplar excepcionalmente preservado de P. tympaniticus conocido como LACM 128319 muestra impresiones de piel, pigmentos alrededor de las fosas nasales, tubos bronquiales y la presencia de una alta aleta caudal

facts.statement: Platecarpus had a long downward-pointing tail with a large dorsal lobe, steering fins, and jaws with aligned conical teeth.
facts.quote: Platecarpus tenía una larga cola orientada hacia abajo con un gran lóbulo dorsal sobre ella, aletas para dirigir el nado, y también mandíbulas con dientes cónicos alineados.

facts.statement: Platecarpus grew up to 4.3 meters in length, with the tail occupying half of that length.
facts.quote: Crecía hasta los 4.3 metros de largo, siendo la mitad de esta longitud ocupada por la cola.

facts.statement: Platecarpus is characterized by a short skull with fewer teeth than other mosasaurs, having approximately 10 teeth in each dentary bone.
facts.quote: Este género se caracteriza por su corto cráneo, en el cual tenía menos dientes que otros mosasaurios (aproximadamente 10 dientes en cada hueso dentario).

facts.statement: Specimen LACM 128319 preserved material within its scleral ring that may represent the eye's retina.
facts.quote: LACM 128319 preservó material dentro de su anillo esclerótico que podría ser la retina del ojo.

facts.statement: Scales on the snout tip and top of the skull were somewhat hexagonal and did not touch each other.
facts.quote: Las escamas en la punta del hocico y en lo alto del cráneo son de forma un tanto hexagonal, sin contacto entre las mismas.

facts.statement: Body scales were all rhomboidal and connected strongly in diagonal rows that overlapped at their posterior edges.
facts.quote: Las escamas del cuerpo son todas romboidales, y se conectan fuertemente en filas diagonales que se superponen unas a otras en sus bordes posteriores.

facts.statement: Caudal scales were taller and larger than those on the rest of the body.
facts.quote: Las escamas caudales son más altas y grandes que las del resto del cuerpo

facts.statement: Part of the digestive tract was preserved and contained fish remains.
facts.quote: Parte del tracto digestivo también se preservó y contiene restos de peces.

facts.statement: Undigested scales and bones in the colon suggest Platecarpus processed food quickly without fully digesting or absorbing it.
facts.quote: La presencia de escamas y huesos no digeridos en el colon, sugieren que Platecarpus y otros mosasaurios procesaban rápidamente la comida sin digerirla o absorbela enteramente en el tubo gastrointestinal.

facts.statement: The tail fin was likely hypocercal, meaning the lower lobe was larger than the upper one.
facts.quote: La aleta caudal probablemente era hipocercal, lo cual significa que el lóbulo inferior era mayor que el superior.

facts.statement: The genus Platecarpus was described by Cope in 1869.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Cope, 1869

facts.statement: Platecarpus lived during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Platecarpus lived approximately 84 to 81 million years ago at the end of the Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: que vivió hace cerca de 84-81 millones de años a finales del período Cretácico.

facts.statement: Fossils of Platecarpus have been found in the United States.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles han sido hallados en Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Platecarpus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: Platecarpus is classified within the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Plioplatecarpinae

facts.statement: The type species of Platecarpus is Platecarpus tympaniticus.
facts.quote: type_species: Platecarpus tympaniticus

facts.statement: It is debated whether Platecarpus swam like an eel or like a modern shark, with recent studies favoring the latter.
facts.quote: Como otros mosasaurios, se pensó inicialmente que nadaba de manera similar a una anguila, aunque un reciente estudio sugiere que nadaba de manera más parecida a los tiburones modernos.

facts.statement: An organ in the abdominal cavity may be a kidney, though it is positioned more anteriorly than in monitor lizards.
facts.quote: El órgano en la cavidad abdominal puede ser un riñón, aunque se sitúa en una posición más anterior que los riñones de los lagartos varanos

facts.statement: The anterior position of the kidneys may have been an adaptation for a more hydrodynamic body.
facts.quote: Esta posición anterior de los riñones pudo haber sido una adaptación para tener un cuerpo más hidrodinámico

facts.statement: Although several fossil skeletons have been found in Kansas deposits, only one complete skull has been recovered for Platecarpus.
facts.quote: Varios esqueletos fósiles de mosasaurio han sido hallados en los depósitos fósiles de Kansas, sin embargo, solo un cráneo completo ha sido recuperado.

facts.statement: Platecarpus fossils are found in rocks dating from the late Coniacian to early Campanian in the Smoky Hill Chalk.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Platecarpus han sido hallados en rocas que datan desde finales del Coniaciense hasta principios del Campaniense en la Caliza de Smoky Hill.

facts.statement: Later studies indicate that Platecarpus is a paraphyletic genus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los estudios posteriores indican que este es un género parafilético.

facts.statement: In 2011, paleontologists Takuya Konishi and Michael W. Caldwell created the new genus Plesioplatecarpus to include P. planifrons, which was determined to be distinct from Platecarpus in a phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: En 2011, un nuevo nombre de género, Plesioplatecarpus, fue acuñado por Takuya Konishi y Michael W. Caldwell para incorporar a P. planifrons, el cual fue determinado como distinto de Platecarpus en un análisis filogenético.

facts.statement: Platecarpus is currently considered monotypic, with the species P. coryphaeus and P. ictericus synonymized with its type species, P. tympaniticus.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Platecarpus es considerado como monotípico y las especies P. coryphaeus y P. ictericus fueron sinonimizadas con su especie tipo, P. tympaniticus.

facts.statement: Compared to tilosaurs, plioplatecarpine mosasaurs had less robust teeth, suggesting they fed on smaller or softer prey such as fish and squid.
facts.quote: Comparado a los tilosaurios, los mosasaurios plioplatecarpinos tenían dientes menos robustos, lo que sugiere que se alimentaban de presas más pequeñas (o más blandas) como peces y calamares.

facts.statement: While it was traditionally thought that mosasaurs propelled themselves through water with a lateral body undulation similar to eels or sea snakes, the large tail fin of Platecarpus suggests it swam more like a shark.
facts.quote: Aunque tradicionalmente se pensaba que los mosasaurios se propulsaban a través del agua con un a ondulación lateral del cuerpo similar a la de las anguilas o las serpientes marinas, la gran aleta caudal de Platecarpus sugiere que nadaba más bien como un tiburón.

facts.statement: This swimming method is known as carangiform locomotion.
facts.quote: Este método de natación es conocido como locomoción carangiforme.

facts.statement: Downward-turned caudal vertebrae in Platecarpus suggest it had a crescent-shaped tail fin.
facts.quote: Las vértebras caudales de Platecarpus vueltas hacia abajo sugieren que tenía una aleta caudal en forma de medialuna.

facts.statement: Neural spines on these vertebrae had grooves for the insertion of interspinous ligaments and dorsal connective tissues which may have helped in the lateral movement of the fin.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales de estas vértebras tenían surcos para la inserción de ligamentos interespinales y tejidos conectivos dorsales los cuales pudieron haber ayudado en el movimiento lateral de la aleta.

facts.statement: The ligaments were likely made of collagen fibers that acted as springs to move the tail back to a resting position once energy was stored in them.
facts.quote: Los ligamentos estaban probablemente hechos de fibras de colágeno que actuaban como resortes para mover la cola de regreso a una posición de descanso una vez que la energía se almacenara en ellos.

facts.statement: While the fin and rear part of the tail of Platecarpus undulated, the base of the tail remained stable.
facts.quote: Mientras que la aleta y la parte posterior de la cola del Platecarpus se ondulaban, la base de la cola permanecía estable.

facts.statement: The structure of Platecarpus scales may have been an adaptation for marine life.
facts.quote: La estructura de las escamas de Platecarpus pudo haber sido una adaptación para la vida marina.

facts.statement: The small size and similar shape of these scales across the body may have kept the body rigid, making it more resistant to lateral movement.
facts.quote: El pequeño tamaño y forma similar de estas escamas a través del cuerpo pudo haber mantenido rígido el cuerpo, haciéndolo más resistente al movimiento lateral.
